elena (OrbitPay): Hey team, started seeing a flood of 429s from your API ~10:15 UTC and then responses started returning very short, garbled results. Our app also shows doubled billing for the same request id. Request id: req_0a7f3c. Any idea?

sara: Sorry about that — can you paste a full request/response pair and timestamp? Are you in EU region or APAC?

elena (OrbitPay): We're EU customers but the app reported a zone failover to apac-standby at 10:14:57. Sample payload (masked):
```
POST /v1/generate
{"model": "rw-infer-standard-3b", "input": "Summarize invoice 8932...", "user": "orbitpay-frontend"}
```
Response body we got: `"output": "<unk>\n"` and `model: rw-infer-stby-2b-q4` in the X-Model header. Tokenizer mismatch also showed unknown tokens and length much shorter.

ops-bot: [ALERT] region-failover triggered for eu-west-2 -> apac-sg at 2026-03-15T10:14:57Z; cause: auth-probe retry spike from host orbitpay-frontend-01. Fallback profile: standby-quantized.

devon: I'm on it. Early hypothesis: auth retry cascade caused smart-routing to use standby pool in APAC which hosts a quantized 2B variant (rw-infer-stby-2b-q4) that uses a different BPE config. That would explain tokenizer drift and shorter outputs. Billing doubling could be from duplicate retries (frontend retried on 429).

rahul: Confirming: standby pool config for apac-sg differs. Tokenizer file in deployment: `tokenizer_bpe_v2.json` vs prod `tokenizer_bpe_v3.json`. Model capability (context handling / stop tokens) is slightly different — not production-equivalent.

sara: Elena, can you share the client retry policy and raw headers for two consecutive calls? We need to confirm duplicate charge path and whether all retries got logged on our side.

elena (OrbitPay): Headers: `X-Request-Id: req_0a7f3c`, `X-Retry-Count: 1`, `Authorization: Bearer **redacted**`. We see two successful 200s for same id in our logs but different model headers.

devon: Looking at infra logs: I can see the incoming connection from your IP hit eu-west-2 auth gateway, auth probe escalated (401 -> retried auth), gateway policy forwarded to standby route after TTL expiry. Two acceptances recorded at 10:15:04 and 10:15:06 to two different backends (eu-prod-01 and apac-stby-04). We route by session affinity but probe fallback can force cross-region.

rahul: Runtime note: quantized variant returns truncated tokens for some stop sequences unless tokenizer matches. We also have a known issue where the fallback mapping doesn't assert tokenizer equality before swapping model variant. That's a bug.

sara: Action plan: 1) Sara will disable cross-region fallback for the affected customer by policy flag; 2) Devon will roll back routing policy to avoid APAC standby for EU tenants until we reconcile tokenizer parity; 3) Rahul will add a runtime guard to compare tokenizer hash on failover and avoid swapping to incompatible variants.

ops-bot: [ACTION CREATED] incident/INC-2026-0315-01 assigned to devon, rahul; priority P1.

elena (OrbitPay): Appreciate the quick triage. For mitigation, we'd like a temporary allowlist to keep all our traffic pinned to eu-prod pool.

sara: Done — pinned orbitpay org to eu-prod pool and disabled cross-region failover for your org id. Please verify traffic now.

elena (OrbitPay): Verified — no more 429s after pinning and outputs look normal. Billing duplicates stopped.

rahul: Follow-ups: will push a hotfix to runtime guard within next 6 hours, and start a compatibility audit across standby pools to sync tokenizer files and model config.

devon: I'll open a routing policy PR to make failover require tokenizer hash equality and a capability-level check before swapping.

sara: I'll update the support ticket and inflate monitoring alert thresholds to catch replayed retries earlier.

audit-bot: [LOG] incident/INC-2026-0315-01 created by sara at 2026-03-15T10:20:00Z; tags: failover, tokenizer-drift, billing-duplication.

sara: Closing thread for now — owners assigned. Will post the postmortem link when available. :white_check_mark:
